mappings.note: The student must read the data table and state the prediction the established pattern supports - LO-7, prediction plus the reasoning that leads to it. Not LO-6: the question is already framed for them, they only have to reason to the answer.
Contrasts what a theory does (explains why) with what a law does (describes the pattern) - the core discrimination of LO-4.

Requires recognising atomic theory as the chapter's worked example of a theory rather than a law or principle - LO-4 tested by example identification, with all three distractors drawn from the other two categories.
Names the third member of the law/theory/principle trio - the 'offering broad guidance' clause of LO-4. Distractors are guesses and hypotheses, so the test is category discrimination.
Value of a rough estimate is to judge whether a result is reasonable - the cross-check clause of LO-9. Not LO-7: nothing about a future outcome is being anticipated.
Directly about theories staying open to revision as evidence arrives - LO-5. Kept off C8.2-LO-8 because no prediction has failed here; the item is about the standing status of knowledge.
The matching item runs law/theory/principle (LO-4) but adds Model as a fourth term, which only LO-7 defines. Both are needed to complete the match.
Statements 2-3 are prediction-from-evidence (LO-7); statement 4, which the key requires, is that a matching prediction grows confidence - LO-8 word for word. Both must be held to pick option B.

Scored by actually running the rate (2200 kcal against 350 kcal per 100 g) and rejecting answers off by a factor of ten - the 'estimates using rates and assumed values' clause of LO-9, not merely the reasonableness talk of its siblings.

The task is converting a vague claim into questions that measurable data can settle - LO-6. Its neighbour item about reading the humidity table is LO-7, because there the reasoning, not the framing, is tested.
Growth of tiny initial differences in a complex system is LO-10 exactly. Not LO-8: no prediction has been checked against an outcome, the item is about why certainty decays.
Failure treated as a prompt to re-examine rather than to dismiss is LO-8; the item then generalises to theories being correctable, which is LO-5. Both clauses appear in the key.
Assertion is revisability (LO-5); the reason is false because revision follows evidence, not opinion. Stays on LO-5 rather than LO-8 since no prediction or measurement is involved.

Unlike the earlier eclipse item, which asked how science would evaluate the claim (LO-6), this one asks why the claim actually fails - scientific thinking applied to a social belief, C5.2-LO-4, with LO-6 secondary for the absent mechanism test.
A single artefact needing physics, chemistry and biology together is the 'real problem that needs more than one branch' of LO-3. Not LO-4: every field named is a science.
Scored by knowing which branch owns which aspect of the mask, i.e. that the branches are a human division of one problem - LO-3 applied at the discrimination level.
Recommends the rough estimate as the early-reasoning check on whether a result makes sense - LO-9. The distractors are about precision and experiment, so no other outcome is in play.
Why estimation is worth learning - intuition and error detection, the cross-check purpose named in LO-9.

Statement 2 is the reasonableness check (LO-9); statement 3, also required by the key, is that estimation links science to everyday questions - scientific thinking outside science, C5.2-LO-4. That third statement is what separates this from its estimation siblings.
Model B is chosen because it drops what does not affect motion (LO-7), and the stem fixes the purpose - time over a straight-line distance - which is what makes those details droppable (LO-8).
The branches as artificial constructs rather than natural boundaries is the first clause of LO-3. Distractors assert real boundaries, so the whole item turns on that clause.
Assertion needs integration across disciplines and the reason falsely compartmentalises nature - both halves are LO-3's man-made-divisions claim.
Matching each discipline to its contribution to one artefact - LO-3 at the mapping level. Mathematics appears only as a modelling contributor, not as an equation, so C5.2-LO-7 is not engaged.

Statements 2-3 are science as a collective human activity across cultures (LO-5); statement 4, also in the key, is scientific thinking used to evaluate everyday information (LO-4). Both are required by option B.
The diagram's fault is quantities expressed in inconsistent units - LO-6. The distractor about wrong equations is what rules out C5.2-LO-7; the mathematics was fine, the units were not.
